transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I can’t think straight anymore or make simple decisions at work or school, and it’s starting to scare me. I just feel so foggy all the time, and even the smallest tasks feel completely overwhelming.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or a major change in your life recently?

Yes, it really started about a year ago when I began working full-time at the clinic while starting my nursing classes. We had a severe staffing shortage, which turned what should have been a supported orientation into weeks of back-to-back shifts and overwhelming responsibility. That completely threw off my routines and started this downward spiral.
Along with feeling foggy and overwhelmed, have you also been feeling consistently sad or down, or have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes, most days I feel like there's a heavy, gray cloud sitting on my chest, leaving me feeling sad and hopeless for no clear reason. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like my evening jogs and knitting projects, and now I just spend my days off lying in bed scrolling on my phone and ignoring my friends.
Apart from feeling sad and overwhelmed, do you also experience constant, excessive worry about everyday things that you find very difficult to control?

I don't really experience constant or uncontrollable worry about general everyday things. It's more that my mind races specifically about the mistakes I've made at work, falling behind in my schoolwork, and just feeling completely overwhelmed by everything.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since these feelings started?

Yes, both have changed a lot. I have almost no appetite and often survive shifts on just coffee because the thought of food makes me nauseous, so my scrubs are starting to hang off me. When I try to sleep, my mind races for hours about my mistakes, so I don't drift off until around 3 a.m. and wake up constantly feeling completely unrefreshed.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling deeply down, hopeless, or losing interest in things at any point in your life before this started a year ago?
No, I don't think I have ever felt this way before. This past year is really the first time I've ever experienced anything like this.
Sometimes when people feel as hopeless and overwhelmed as you've described, they might have thoughts of self-harm or suicide. Have you experienced any thoughts like that?

Yes, on my worst nights when I'm overwhelmed by unfinished assignments and work stress, I catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up the next morning. It really scares me that those kinds of thoughts are actually starting to make sense to me.
Have you ever had periods lasting a few days or more where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, needing very little sleep, or feeling extremely high or wired?

No, I've never experienced anything like that at all. My struggle has been completely the opposite—just feeling incredibly heavy, tired, and down all the time. I've never had periods where I felt unusually energetic or wired.
To help me understand the full picture, do you have any medical conditions, such as thyroid issues, or are you currently taking any medications or using any substances?

No, I don't have any other medical conditions like thyroid issues, and I'm not taking any medications. I don't use any substances either, though I do rely heavily on coffee just to get through my shifts at the clinic.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time depressive episode lasting approximately one year, characterized by persistent depressed mood, marked anhedonia, significant sleep disturbance (onset and maintenance insomnia), decreased appetite with noticeable weight loss, cognitive difficulties (brain fog and indecisiveness), and passive suicidal ideation. These symptoms began in the context of significant occupational and academic stress but have persisted and meet the threshold for a moderate depressive episode. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and no substance use or medical conditions (e.g., thyroid issues) explaining the symptoms.
